inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 CONTINUING revenue (BTP Group reclassified to discontinued; underlying incl. BTP was 3,463.2). The forward build is continuing-only; BTP's sale proceeds sit in equity_bridge.
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average shares adjusted for dilution, FY2026 annual report note 5 (936.6m basic + 23.3m share rights = 959.9m). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. Buybacks (A$13.1m FY26, incl. A$2.9m of on-market purchases for share awards) are the mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings 549.443 (USD notes 505.8 + secured 51.0 + NCI loan 1.2 - capitalised costs 8.5) less cash 322.524, EX lease liabilities (21.866) because leases are charged inside the flows (treatment B). Company-reported net debt incl. leases is 248.785. Balance sheet 30 June 2026.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income was A$4.7m (interest received A$2.9m) but Perenti is a net-debt company (A$227m ex-lease), so no interest-income strip applies; the cash pile is netted against debt, not added to EV.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report cash-flow reconciliation / share-based payments expense (A$9.404m); no separate equity-award tax line disclosed (net-share settlement not used; shares for awards are bought on-market, A$2.9m in FY26, already in buyback_cash).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:15:45Z (intraday ASX print; ASX session closes 06:00Z, replace at the regular close if it moves)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: AU 10y government ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.3 for a capex-heavy, gold-cycle-exposed contractor = ~11.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~7% (USD notes) = ~4.9% after tax; ~80/20 E/D at market gives ~10.2%. One 10.0% WACC on all three scenarios; cyclicality, African sovereign risk and the CEO transition are charged in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: B: leases as operating cost. Full lease payment (A$14.5m principal, FY26 cash-flow statement, + ~A$1.5m lease interest on A$21.9m of liabilities) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path (0.5% of revenue); lease liabilities EXCLUDED from net_debt. D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: NCI share of profit (A$25.3m FY26, ~24% of continuing NPAT, from African partner-held subsidiaries) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax + minority leakage rate (38% of EBIT in FY27, easing to 36% as Africa mix shrinks). NCI equity (A$57.3m) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge. Calibration: FY0 modelled NOPAT ~A$175m vs continuing attributable NPAT A$81.9m + after-tax net interest ~A$37m + impairments A$54m + one-offs ~A$10m = ~A$183m, ties within noise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with the adaptations file applied: AUD-built WACC, lease treatment B, NCI folded into leakage, mid-cycle margin normalisation, single WACC. Perenti is a contract mining and drilling services operating company, ~76% gold and ~8% copper exposed; it has real FCF, real net debt and no fair-value or deposit distortions, so the owner-FCF engine applies. MID-CYCLE: FY26 is a record underlying EBIT(A) year at record gold prices, so the base case glides the cash EBITDA margin from the FY26 continuing level (18.3% ex-impairment; 18.8% on the company's underlying definition, which also strips idoba product development and FX losses that this model treats as real costs) to a 17.5% mid-cycle level (FY20-FY26 average ~17.5%) rather than extrapolating the peak. FY26 reported FCF (OCF - capex = 95.3) is depressed by A$50.9m of FY26 receipts collected in July 2026 and by the capex step-up; the forward flows are margin-built so that receivable reversal is carried in equity_bridge instead. Cash tax rate path is the combined 30% Australian rate + NCI leakage (see nci_treatment); cash taxes paid were A$83m on ~A$300m of pre-impairment EBIT (~28%), so the 30% statutory component is not flattered by the recognised tax losses. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF (cyclical, structurally ~10% EBIT margin, D&A ~ capex). Buyback: repurchaser (A$13.1m FY26, A$25.1m FY25), so the flat count is funded.

equity_bridge.item: BTP Group sale proceeds (A$80m on completion ~Oct 2026 + A$20m deferred 12 months, lightly discounted)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR note 20; BTP held for sale at 30 June 2026 (net assets ~A$100m). BTP's revenue (A$125m) and EBITDA (A$24.7m) are excluded from the continuing base, so its value enters only here.

equity_bridge.item: FY26 contract-mining receipts of A$50.9m collected July 2026 (abnormal year-end timing)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 remuneration report footnote: 'two receipts of $50.9m collected in July from two contract mining clients in respect of FY26 activity'. Net debt at 30 June is overstated by this relative to steady state; the FY27 margin-built flows do not include the reversal.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment: FY27 guidance midpoint (+5% on continuing revenue) decelerating to 2.5% nominal; equity CAGR overstated by DDH1 scrip issuance (FY24 shares 716m -> 908m) and FY19 revenue base pre-dates Barminco full-year consolidation
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue CAGRs (5.0% 3y / 9.8% 5y on FY26 continuing revenue) include the FY24 DDH1 acquisition; EPS 3y CAGR is negative because FY26 continuing diluted EPS (8.6c) carries A$54m of impairments and FY21 EPS was negative (5y n/a); owner-FCF CAGRs (94% 3y / 41% 5y) are trough-to-recovery arithmetic from FY21 (A$15.6m) and FY23 (A$11.7m) fleet-renewal years and describe nothing about the forward rate. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC, no interest strip as the company is net-debt) is A$85.9m FY26 vs A$190.1m FY25: SBC is small (0.3% of revenue) so the owner and reported series move together; the FY26 drop is capex timing and the A$50.9m July receipt, not SBC.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC). SBC is ~0.3% of revenue, so the owner-vs-reported gap is immaterial; SBC is NOT growing faster than cash flow.

base.growth_note: FY27 +5.0% on continuing revenue = A$3,505m, low-mid of the A$3.45-3.65bn underlying guidance range (the range still carries ~4 months of BTP). Fourmile and Bellevue ramp, Iduapriem exits mid-FY27. Decelerates to 2.5% nominal (mining-services volume growth ~ inflation over a cycle).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Cash EBITDA margin pre-IFRS-16-lease (lease charged separately). FY26 continuing: 18.3% ex-impairments, 18.8% on company underlying definition. FY27 guidance EBIT(A) A$335-355m on A$3.45-3.65bn implies ~18.4-18.7% EBITDA; base holds 18.3% then glides to the FY20-26 mid-cycle average of ~17.5% by year 5 because FY26 is a record-gold-price year.
base.da_note: FY26 continuing D&A 319.3 (9.6% of revenue) less ~15 right-of-use depreciation = ~9.1%; includes 28.2 of customer-related-intangible amortisation (~0.85pp) that rolls off by ~FY29 (remaining CRI ~A$47m), hence the glide to 8.8%.
base.capex_note: Net of routine fleet disposal proceeds (A$27.6m FY26, A$86.5m FY25). FY27 guided gross capex ~A$370m (incl. ~4 months BTP) less ~A$30m disposals = ~A$340m = 9.7% of A$3,505m. Long run settles ~0.2-0.4pp above D&A ex-CRI (8.8%) to fund 2.5% growth. History (gross/revenue): FY22 19.2%, FY23 13.0%, FY24 10.0%, FY25 8.9%, FY26 10.4%.
base.cash_tax_note: Combined leakage on EBIT: 30% tax + ~8pp NCI share (A$25.3m FY26 on ~A$300m pre-impairment EBIT), easing to 36% as the Africa mix (source of the NCI) shrinks. See inputs.nci_treatment.
base.wc_note: Contractor: receivables (~15% of revenue) exceed payables (~10%), so growth consumes ~7% of the revenue increase. Negative capture.
base.narrative: Gold and copper capex stays supportive but not euphoric. FY27 lands inside guidance (revenue ~A$3.5bn, EBIT(A) ~A$340m); Fourmile and Bellevue ramp offsets the Iduapriem exit and BTP disposal. Margins ease from the FY26 record back to the FY20-26 mid-cycle average of ~17.5% EBITDA as the gold-price tailwind normalises; capex runs a little above depreciation to fund low-single-digit growth. Owner FCF settles at ~4-4.5% of revenue, ~A$150-180m, and the terminal value is capped at 12x that.

bull.narrative: Top of FY27 guidance (revenue ~A$3.62bn continuing, EBIT(A) at or above A$355m) and the A$20bn tender pipeline converts: North America scales beyond Fourmile, Bellevue-sized Australian awards repeat, drilling utilisation keeps rising. Tier-one mix lifts margins toward 19% and shrinks the NCI leakage (Africa) to ~4pp. Capex runs higher to fund the growth. Gold stays above US$4,000 through the horizon.

bear.narrative: FY27 misses the bottom of guidance as Iduapriem exits early and the CEO transition slows tendering; then a gold/copper price reversal in FY28-29 cuts client development capex, revenue falls ~10% over two years and the EBITDA margin drops to a FY22-like 15% as fixed fleet costs and mobilisation costs bite. Further African policy shocks (Ghana precedent) remove more work and the NCI/withholding leakage rises. Capex is cut below depreciation during the trough (fleet idled), then recovers. Margins recover only to 16.5%, never back to the FY26 record; terminal growth 2%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 30% because ~76% of revenue is gold-linked and FY26 is a record-gold-price, record-earnings year (mean reversion is the base risk, not a tail), ~37% of revenue still sits in West/Southern Africa where the Ghana exits show contract loss is a live pattern, and a new CEO started May 2026. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things at once: gold holding at records, pipeline conversion at tier-one margins, and NCI leakage shrinking. No going-concern or covenant risk (0.4x leverage, A$911m liquidity), so bear is not higher.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Perenti is a capital-intensive, price-taking mining-services contractor valued on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the FY26 record underlying EBIT(A). The engine converts a ~18% EBITDA margin into only ~4-4.5% owner-FCF margin because depreciation is ~9% of revenue and fleet capex must run at or above it, and because ~8pp of EBIT leaks to African minority partners. The stock screens cheap on P/E (~11x NPAT(A)) and EV/EBITDA (~3.8x) precisely because so little EBITDA reaches shareholders as free cash. BTP's A$100m sale proceeds and the A$50.9m July receivable are added in the bridge rather than in the flows. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (cyclical); one 10% AUD WACC; risk lives in the bear flows and the 30% bear weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold/copper price reversal cutting client development capex (76% of revenue gold-linked; FY26 margins are a cyclical high)
African sovereign/policy risk: Iduapriem (Ghana) forced exit and Ghana Manganese loss are precedents; ~37% of revenue and all of the NCI leakage sit there
Capex intensity: FY27 guided ~A$370m gross; if sustaining capex proves structurally above depreciation, owner FCF margin is below the 4-4.5% modelled
Statutory vs underlying gap: FY26 statutory NPAT A$18.8m vs NPAT(A) A$192.1m; impairments (A$54m) and BTP loss (A$64m) recur in some form most years for this group
CEO transition (Vanessa Torres from May 2026) during the Fourmile/Bellevue ramp
Terminal cap and WACC: the 12x cap binds in base and bull; each 1pp of WACC is worth roughly A$0.20-0.25/share
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_banner: Multiples sanity check tripped on implied P/E (214x vs a 45x 10-year average). Both figures are artefacts of FY26 statutory EPS of 2.0c, which carries the A$63.1m BTP discontinued-operations loss and A$54.3m of non-cash impairments; on FY26 underlying NPAT(A) of A$192.1m (~20c/share) the base IV of A$2.09 is ~10.4x, inside the FY19-FY25 P/E range of 6.7-15.2x, and on continuing diluted EPS of 8.6c (still after impairments) it is ~24x. Implied EV/EBITDA 4.1x (hist. avg 3.3x, max 4.4x) and P/B 1.10x (hist. max 1.11x) are inside their ranges. Fix pass applied: the peak-FCF diagnosis is already handled by construction (forward flows are margin-built at the FY20-26 mid-cycle EBITDA margin of 17.5%, not extrapolated from the A$85.9m base-year FCF; 12x terminal cap; 30% bear weight). No WACC premium was added because cyclicality and African policy risk are charged in the bear flows and weights, and stacking a premium would charge them twice. The valuation already sits BELOW the current price (weighted IV A$2.02 vs A$2.195).
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_status: tripped on statutory-EPS P/E only; explained above; not re-looped
